plan.title: Gradient descent on a quadratic bowl
plan.description: A bowl-shaped surface shows the loss L(x, y) = ½(x² + c·y²), with contour lines and its lowest point marked at the centre. A ball sits at a starting point. With each step it moves against the gradient (the direction in which the loss rises fastest), and a trail records its path. An arrow on the ball shows the next step: its direction, and a length equal to learning rate × gradient size. Readouts show the step number, the current loss and the gradient size, so you can watch the loss shrink, zig-zag or blow up depending on the settings.
plan.reason: Changing the learning rate and the bowl's steepness, then watching the path, shows directly why a small step creeps along, a medium one converges quickly, and a step that is too large overshoots and diverges.
interactions: Press play or step to move the ball one gradient step at a time; the trail grows and the readouts update.
Change the learning rate: small values give a slow, smooth path; values near 1/c make the path zig-zag across the narrow direction; values above 2/c make it bounce outward and diverge.
Change the steepness: c = 1 gives a round bowl and a straight path to the centre; larger c gives a narrow valley and a curved or zig-zag path.
Drag the ball to a new starting point on the surface.
Use 'Restart from start point' to clear the trail and step count but keep your current settings and starting point.
assumptions: Illustration: a simple two-variable quadratic bowl, not the loss of a trained model.
Each step is exactly: x ← x − η·x and y ← y − η·c·y, where η is the learning rate. That is plain gradient descent with no momentum and no noise.
Because the loss is quadratic, each coordinate shrinks by a fixed factor every step: (1 − η) along x and (1 − η·c) along y. It converges exactly when both factors lie strictly between −1 and 1.
The run stops when the gradient size falls below 0.01, after 100 steps, or when the ball leaves the drawn surface. The last case is reported as 'diverged'.
Default start is x = −2.5, y = 1.5.
limitations: Real loss surfaces have many dimensions and are not perfect bowls. This shows only the two-variable quadratic case, where gradient descent always succeeds or always fails in a predictable way.
Once a diverging path leaves the drawn area it is no longer shown. Only the 'diverged' outcome is reported.
plan.learningGoal: Understand that gradient descent repeatedly steps opposite the gradient, and that the learning rate relative to the bowl's steepness decides whether the path converges smoothly, oscillates or diverges.

draft.title: Gradient descent on a quadratic bowl
draft.description: A blue bowl-shaped surface shows the loss L(x, y) = ½(x² + c·y²). It has contour lines, and a dark dot marks its lowest point at the centre. A red ball starts at x = −2.5, y = 1.5, and a green pin marks the start. Each gradient step moves the ball against the gradient, and an orange trail records every step. An orange arrow on the ball shows the next step. Readouts show the loss, the gradient size, the step count and the status. A larger c makes the bowl narrower along y.

actions.label: Restart from start point, keep old path

assumptions: Illustration: a simple two-variable quadratic bowl, not the loss of a trained model.

Each step is exactly x ← x − η·x, y ← y − η·c·y (plain gradient descent, no momentum, no noise). Each coordinate shrinks by (1 − η) along x and (1 − η·c) along y, so the run converges exactly when η < 2/c (e.g. η < 0.667 at c = 3).
The run stops when the gradient size falls below 0.01 (converged), when the ball leaves the drawn surface (diverged), or after 100 steps (stopped). Default start: x = −2.5, y = 1.5.
Height is drawn at 0.2 × loss. The drawn surface spans x in ±3.6 and y in ±3.6/√c, so it narrows as c grows. The readouts give the true loss.
The orange arrow is the next step (−η × gradient), drawn at its true length in x–y units (scale 1). It points downhill, against the gradient.
Drag the ball sideways to set the start x and drag the green pin to set the start y. Either drag starts a new run and keeps the previous path as a faint ghost.
'Restart from start point, keep old path' clears the trail and step count, keeps your settings and start point, and keeps the last path as a ghost for comparison.

findings.message: The 'Start' label sits over the green start pin and crowds the 'Next step' label beside it, so the pin is mostly hidden in the default view. Offset the Start label further from the pin.

The plan's interaction text says learning rates near 1/c make the path zig-zag. In fact η = 1/c sends y to 0 in one step; zig-zag happens for 1/c < η < 2/c and gets stronger towards 2/c. The artifact doesn't repeat the claim, but any wording it adds should say this correctly.

At η = 0.8 (c = 3, start y = 1.5) the first step lands at y = −2.1, beyond the surface edge at about 2.078, so the run reads 'diverged' after one jump and the outward bouncing is not seen. Rates of about 0.67–0.79 should bounce for several steps before leaving, but they weren't sampled.
The diverged ball is drawn just past the far edge of the surface, held there by the host's clamp. This slightly contradicts the plan's limitation that a ball off the drawn area is no longer shown.

blocks.text:
I found no blocker or major problems in the six captures, so all of them pass both the semantic and visual checks. There are four minor findings.

**What checks out:**
- **Formulas match the plan.** The program computes L = ½(x² + c·y²), uses gradient size hypot(x, c·y), and applies the update x ← x − η·x, y ← y − η·c·y, exactly as planned.
- **Readouts match by hand.**
  - Initial state: loss 6.5, gradient size 5.1478.
  - At η = 0.12, c = 3: Run, then 16 steps over 48 ticks, one Step once, then 10 more steps gives step 27. Loss is 0.0031 and gradient size is 0.0792 (from 2.5·0.88²⁷).
  - At η = 0.8: after one step the ball is at (−0.5, −2.1). The surface edge is at |y| = 3.6/√3 ≈ 2.078, so the ball is past it and the status correctly reads "diverged", with loss 6.74.
- **Drawing matches the numbers.** The surface heights are 0.2 × loss: a round grid squeezed along y by 1/√c, as the assumptions say. The step arrow points against the gradient at its true length, and the path's curve (y dies out fast because 0.64 < 0.88, then x creeps in) agrees with the readouts.
- **Controls are unchanged.** Both parameters keep the requested ranges, steps and defaults. Learning rate comes first and loss is the first readout. The bowl fills the default view, and the labels are readable.

**Minor findings:**
1. **Start label covers the pin (default view, initial state).** The "Start" label sits over the green pin, which also crowds the "Next step" label. Moving the label further out would fix it.
2. **Divergence at the top of the range lasts one step.** At η = 0.8 the ball leaves the surface after a single jump, so the learner never sees it bounce outward. Values between about 0.67 and 0.79 should bounce for several steps before leaving, but that range wasn't sampled.
3. **The plan's zig-zag claim is slightly off.** It says rates near 1/c cause zig-zag. In fact η = 1/c sends y to 0 in a single step; zig-zag happens for η between 1/c and 2/c and gets stronger towards 2/c. The artifac
